items.title: Latency vs throughput: ek request kitni der, aur ek second mein kitni
items.one_idea: Latency is how long one request takes from send to answer; throughput is how many requests get done per unit time; they are two different numbers, so a server can answer each request fast and still be overloaded, and the catch is that as load nears the limit, latency climbs.
items.spoken_hook: Fast server भी हज़ारों requests पर अटक सकता है।
items.hook_formula: surprising_fact: a short claim that corrects a belief (fast per request means it handles many); the problem is stated in plain words in the next line, no definition between hook and answer
items.hook_10s: Fast server भी हज़ारों requests पर अटक सकता है। हर request एक second में निपटे, फिर भी एक साथ दस हज़ार आ जाएँ तो? Speed दो तरह की होती है, और हम अक्सर एक ही नापते हैं। [frame 0: one canteen counter, one cup of tea moving across in 2 s, a queue of people waiting behind it]

hook_candidates.text: Fast server भी हज़ारों requests पर अटक सकता है।
Server तेज़ है, तो फिर लोग इंतज़ार क्यों कर रहे हैं?
Interviewer ने पूछा: latency और throughput में फ़र्क़ क्या है?

items.visual_idea: A canteen counter with a queue. A stopwatch above one customer shows the wait for one cup (latency); a tally beside the counter shows cups per minute (throughput). A second counter slides in: the stopwatch stays the same, the tally doubles. Last, the queue grows and the stopwatch number climbs.
items.everyday_anchor: A college canteen or chai counter at lunch: one cup takes the same time to make, but how many people you serve per hour depends on how many counters work at once.
items.example: EXAMPLE (not measured): one counter, 2 minutes per cup = latency 2 min, throughput 30 cups per hour; two counters = latency still 2 min, throughput 60 cups per hour. Arithmetic: 60 / 2 = 30, 30 x 2 = 60.
facts_to_verify: Latency is the delay of communication/one request (AWS: network latency is the delay in network communication; Wikipedia: delay between sender and receiver)
Throughput is the actual rate at which messages are delivered per unit time; bandwidth is the maximum (Wikipedia Network performance and Throughput)
Latency and throughput are different quantities: the Latency (engineering) page says a trip's latency is independent of the throughput of the link
Catch: as a system nears its maximum load, queuing makes latency rise without bound (Wikipedia Throughput, asymptotic throughput section); say 'typically'
Optional one-line link: average items in the system = arrival rate x average time in system (Little's law page); only use if the script needs it
All canteen numbers are EXAMPLE with arithmetic on screen; no real company or measured number is claimed
